name: אֲחַרְחֵל
summary: Aharhel son of Harum is named once, among the clans of Judah: Koz fathered “the families of Aharhel the son of Harum” (1Ch 4:8). Scripture does not explain the name. As it is spelt it divides into אַחַר, “behind”, and חֵל, “rampart”, the outer wall of a city (2Sa 20:15; Lam 2:8): “behind the rampart”. That is only a reading of the spelling; nothing else ties the name to this root, and it may be of another origin altogether.

evidence.note: מִשְׁפְּחֹת אֲחַרְחֵל בֶּן־הָרוּם: “the families of Aharhel the son of Harum”, the only place the name stands.
אַחַר as “behind”: the opening of the tent “was behind him”.
חֵל: the siege mound “stood against the rampart”.

note: Derivation doubtful; the entry is here because the name is filed under this root and a person bears it. The Septuagint is said to read “brother of Rechab” here (as if אֲחִי רֵחָב); MACULA’s alignment leaves the word unaligned and the reading was not checked, so it is not cited. The reviewer may prefer to drop this entry.
